Hi Anita / Mike,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion attached are Redwood's proposed redlines to the MSA (key focus: governing law, dispute resolution, and emergency relief). High level: we preserved SolsticeAI's preference for arbitration for non-injunctive disputes but requested Delaware law for predictability on contract interpretation and a narrow carve for interim equitable relief in the customer's forum when necessary to preserve confidentiality or IP.

Key changes called out in the draft:
- Governing law: Delaware (subparts explain choice and impact on enforceability).
- Arbitration threshold: disputes under $250,000 may go to small-claims-style arbitration; above that, JAMS/AAA arbitration in Delaware.
- Emergency/injunctive relief: Redwood proposes a mutual carve permitting either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in any competent forum to prevent immediate harm (limited to preservation of trade secrets, IP, or access to customer data). We added notice and expedited briefing requirements.
- Service of process & injunctive notice: 10 business days' notice where practicable; emergency relief may be sought sooner with subsequent meet-and-confer within 48 hours.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v4.docx (docx)], [Attachment: OrderForm_SolsticeAI_v2.pdf (pdf)].

Would like to get your read on the injunctive relief carve — you said on the call SolsticeAI legal would be sensitive to broad venue waivers. If you prefer a CA-only carve for provisional relief, please flag the exact language you need and why.

Next steps: if legal is comfortable, we can mirror the language in the order form and circulate for signature via DocuSign.

Thanks,

Naomi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear callouts. High-level feedback from Solstice legal: we are aligned on keeping arbitration as primary path, but SolsticeAI cannot accept Delaware as sole governing law for disputes concerning local regulatory obligations and consumer-facing claims — we'd need California law to apply to those narrow categories.

On emergency relief: we agree a mutual carve is sensible, but must limit it to: (i) preservation of customer data/access, (ii) protection of customer-facing production services, and (iii) injunctive relief as required by applicable privacy/regulatory rule. We cannot accept a catch-all "trade secrets" formulation without further limiting language.

Proposed compromise language (inline):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek preliminary or emergency injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights related to (a) protection or preservation of customer data or production services; (b) compliance with applicable privacy or regulatory obligations; or (c) narrowly-defined IP protection relating to identification and mitigation of unauthorized data exfiltration. Any party seeking such relief shall, where feasible, provide notice and an opportunity to cure; absent feasibility, expedited notice shall follow the emergency filing."

Also flagging procurement note: the order form contains a payment schedule that would push the initial invoice into Q3; Mike will follow up on payment timing.

–Anita
General Counsel, SolsticeAI

Naomi / Laura — thanks for the ping. I reviewed Anita's suggested carve and believe it's workable with two minor edits to protect Redwood's enforcement rights while addressing their regulatory concern:

1) Replace "customer-facing production services" with "customer production services (i.e., services used in customer-facing production environments)" to avoid ambiguity.
2) Add an express reservation that seeking emergency relief in a forum where the regulatory/consumer claim arises does not waive Redwood's right to enforce arbitration for the underlying dispute, and require any emergency relief order to be stayed or converted to arbitration within 30 days if the arbitrator so orders.

Proposed redline paragraph (single-line string for insertion):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may seek preliminary or emergency injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to (i) preserve customer data or access to customer production services (i.e., services used in customer-facing production environments), (ii) protect or enable compliance with applicable privacy or regulatory obligations, or (iii) seek narrowly-tailored IP protection to prevent imminent unauthorized exfiltration of customer data. Such emergency relief shall be limited to the preservation of the status quo and shall not be construed as a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits of any dispute; any emergency relief order shall, upon motion of either party, be stayed and referred to arbitration within 30 days for determination whether the merits are subject to arbitration. The party seeking emergency relief shall provide notice to the other party as soon as practicable and, absent impracticability, at least 48 hours' advance notice and an opportunity to meet-and-confer prior to filing."

From a conflict perspective: Delaware governing law for interpretation of contract terms remains our preferred global position — but carving California for regulatory/consumer claims is acceptable provided the language is narrow and limited to statutory/regulatory obligations. Document the carve in both the MSA and the order form (short cross-reference).

I recommend we send the redline with Karthik's insertion and call out the arbitration-narrowing reservation for Solstice. If they take it, we can proceed to DocuSign.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
